_meta.authority: Director console 2026-08-24, verbatim: "by Friday I want to open the site and see something a customer or a domain expert would care about that isn't there today — PB1, the growth path, Explore's remaining stages with real data" and "I'm handing you the machinery, not asking permission back ... Everything else, decide and go." He named the growth path as the deliverable, so building it and leaving it switched off would be the bare-ask defect NEVER_ASK_WITHOUT_RECOMMENDING.md forbids. What stays reserved is CURRICULUM VALUES, and this file deliberately holds none: it is on/off only, and the size of the book falls out of the company's own balance sheet through company/interfaces/growth_desk.plan_growth_campaign_year(). The 2026-08-11 ruling that minted PB3 assigns the numbers to the worker in its own last line — "sequencing and numbers are the worker's, the ordering and the wall are the director's".
_meta.r13_discipline: Whether this world contains a supplier that runs acquisition campaigns is a CURRICULUM question — which world the company faces — and therefore the director's. HOW BIG a campaign that supplier runs is the company's own decision, made from its own balance sheet through company/interfaces/growth_desk.plan_growth_campaign_year(). The two are deliberately separated: this file is on/off, and it holds no growth number at all.

activated.basis: Flipped 2026-08-24 after a full run measured green at 8.5 min. Prior state: false, for the length of one commit (b8081a60f). REVERT is this one field: set it back to false and the next publish cycle returns the 20-record book and net £1,529,289 exactly, because with the flag off simulation/net_new_acquisition.py is never called at all.
activated.effect: simulation.live_population.live_population() appends the accounts a ten-year acquisition campaign actually WON — each one having survived the five-stage funnel, the credit check and the statutory cooling-off window — and registers them on the supply book. live_premises()/live_drawn_households() carry the world's dwelling for each won home, so the company can still be wrong about it (B12).

measured_when_on.basis: Full run at base seed 20260724, measured 2026-08-24 before the flag was offered. These are OUTCOMES, not settings: nothing in this file or in the code targets them.
measured_when_on.realised_conversion: 5.7% of quotes issued became accounts, against the funnel's own ~19% on an unconstrained pool — the gap is wins the settlement cap refused, and they were still billed
measured_when_on.years_that_won_nothing: 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024, 2025 — growth is contingent, which is the property clause 3 asks for
measured_when_on.binding_constraint: settlement_engine from 2019 onward. NOT the balance sheet: the supplier's capital supports ~900 new accounts in year one. See simulation/net_new_acquisition.py::SETTLEMENT_CUSTOMER_YEAR_BUDGET.

known_limitations.electricity_only: A won gas account's record needs an aq_kwh the drawn saas-shaped dict does not carry, and run_phase2b.TOTAL_GAS_AQ raises KeyError on the first one. Inventing an annual quantity for a home whose gas nothing has modelled is worse than single-fuel growth. Dual-fuel net-new is real remaining work.
known_limitations.domestic_only: The whole plan is denominated in Ofgem's MCR, which is a per-domestic-customer figure. An SME prospect also has no drawn dwelling, so it would raise DwellingNotDrawn.
known_limitations.no_competitor: The loss side is the funnel's own leakage, not a rival supplier's counter-offer. B4_competitor_field is PB3's named couple and is a separate atom.
known_limitations.no_forecast_contribution: The plan spends down from capital held and does not credit itself with margin the new accounts will earn, so the modelled ceiling is conservative. See saas/growth_mandate.py.

published_figures_moved.notice: The director's standing instruction on the sibling activation is 'Tell me before any published figure moves, and re-baseline honestly'. He was told by NTFY on 2026-08-24 before this flip reached a publish cycle.
published_figures_moved.book: 20 records (14 accounts + 5 gas legs + 1 SYN) -> 34 records; 14 net-new electricity accounts won from 245 quotes
published_figures_moved.why_it_fell: Growth costs money. 245 quotes were paid for and 231 of them lost, and a decade of acquisition spend against thin new-account margin is a real supplier result rather than a defect. A reader who sees the book grow and the margin fall is seeing the actual trade a small supplier makes.
published_figures_moved.run_cost: 3,226,200 settlement periods, 8.5 min against ~5 min at the 20-record book. Publishing cadence is unaffected: the cycle is dominated by the publish gate, not the sim.
